findings.title: build.yaml artifacts omits build.yaml, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and licenses/
findings.detail: artifacts lists ArrTags.dll, SkiaSharp.dll, libSkiaSharp.so, ArrTags.deps.json, but the produced zip also carries build.yaml, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and the three licenses/ notices. The mismatch is a pre-existing repository convention (the custom PackagePlugin target ships the extra files) and is explicitly disclosed in the worker report. It is harmless for this repository because build.yaml is not consumed by the Jellyfin local loader (PluginManifest has no artifacts property; no host source references it). It would only matter if packaging moved to jprm/repository tooling, where the notices would be dropped unless added to artifacts. Not a task 5.4 acceptance gap: the notices are present in the plugin zip and verified by hash.

findings.title: Shipped ArrTags.deps.json still references runtimes/linux-x64/native while the native asset is flattened to the root
findings.detail: Independently confirmed harmless. A fresh extraction plus a replica resolver showed AssemblyDependencyResolver(pluginFolder) resolves neither managed SkiaSharp nor libSkiaSharp (null/null), and AssemblyDependencyResolver(pluginFolder/ArrTags.dll) resolves managed SkiaSharp.dll but returns null for the unmanaged name. The effective mechanism is Jellyfin's explicit LoadFromAssemblyPath folder DLL scan plus the runtime's same-directory native probing, so the root-level libSkiaSharp.so is the one loaded. The worker's stated limitation is accurate and does not hide a gap.

findings.title: Package-content tests do not run in the standard `./build.sh test`/`all` flow
findings.detail: The three [PackagedPluginFact] facts skip unless artifacts/ArrTags_*.zip already exists, and build.sh all runs test before package, so archive-content assertions are skipped in the normal flow and only run if `./build.sh package` is executed first (as the README documents). The five unguarded facts are contract/text assertions and do not functionally prove the archive. This is a test-ergonomics weakness, not an acceptance gap: the real archive was independently rebuilt and its nine entries hash-verified, including the pinned managed/native SHA-256 values from the test constants.

findings.title: Live host did not invoke the renderer; native resolution confirmed indirectly and reproduced by this review
findings.detail: The pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host log at 2026-09-19 22:26 records `Loaded assembly "SkiaSharp, Version=3.119.0.0, ..." from .../ArrTags_0.1.0.0/SkiaSharp.dll`, `Loaded plugin: "ArrTags" "0.1.0.0"`, and reaches startup completion; the extracted host plugin folder and meta.json (targetAbi 12.0.0.0, status Active, assemblies []) match the package. The host could not exercise a render because 5.5/5.11 are not implemented. Reviewer independently reproduced the byte-for-byte PluginLoadContext replica over a fresh extraction: with the host managed+native SkiaSharp preloaded, the plugin ALC loaded SkiaSharp.dll and ArrTags.dll from the plugin folder, the plugin-context decode/encode succeeded (134-byte PNG), and /proc/self/maps showed the plugin-folder libSkiaSharp.so and the host libSkiaSharp.so as two distinct inode mappings. Task 5.4 acceptance (packaging + resolution under the plugin load context) is satisfied to the extent possible before 5.5/5.11.

findings.title: Zip is not byte-for-byte reproducible
findings.detail: MSBuild ZipDirectory records source timestamps, so archive bytes differ between runs although every entry content hash is identical. Reproducible packaging is a Milestone 7 exit-gate concern, not a 5.4 requirement; the limitation is disclosed.

findings.title: architecture.md refers to build.yaml as `the plugin manifest`
findings.detail: Terminology nit only. build.yaml is the build/repository manifest; the runtime manifest Jellyfin reads is meta.json. The surrounding statement is otherwise accurate and matches the measured load-context behavior.
